title: Setup refuses before launching login when there is no terminal, and names the way out
statement: With stdin not a TTY and no usable authentication already present, setup refuses BEFORE starting the interactive login step — verified by the login process never being spawned, not merely by the message printed — and prints both supported recovery routes: run setup from a local interactive terminal, or configure authentication on the target host outside Kiln and rerun with the required non-interactive decisions. With usable authentication already present, the same non-TTY invocation proceeds instead of refusing.
notes: ⚠️ THE PROCESS-NEVER-SPAWNED HALF IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS. A refusal message printed just before launching the TUI anyway would satisfy a text assertion and still hang a CI job, which is the failure this exists to prevent — a hang is indistinguishable from work until a timeout. ⚠️ AND THE SECOND ROW IS A CONTROL: if the non-TTY path refused unconditionally, the refusal would prove nothing about TTY detection.
